project: CropHealth AI - Early Crop Stress Detection
description: Standardized schema manifest and dataset protocol for multimodal satellite crop stress detection.
target_task: Multi-class classification of potential vegetative stress signals from combined Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical time-series.

0.name: No significant stress signal detected
0.description: Nominal vegetative canopy health, stable or increasing multi-spectral vigor, and normal structural backscatter.
0.criteria: Healthy canopy trajectory with no statistically significant radiometric or structural decline across consecutive observation passes.

1.name: Potential stress signal detected
1.description: Early radiometric or polarimetric anomaly indicating potential early vegetative strain.
1.criteria: Subtle decrease in moisture (NDMI) or red-edge chlorophyll (NDRE) preceding severe NDVI collapse, or anomalous radar cross-polarization ratio shift.

2.name: Elevated potential stress signal
2.description: Marked, concurrent decline across spectral and structural canopy indicators.
2.criteria: Simultaneous drops in vigor (NDVI/EVI), moisture (NDMI), and red-edge (NDRE) alongside persistent SAR volumetric backscatter loss over >1 observation cycle.

provenance_requirements.geographic_bounds: WGS84 Bounding Box and GeoJSON Polygon
provenance_requirements.crop_type: Documented crop species (e.g., paddy rice, maize, wheat, cotton, soybean)
provenance_requirements.label_source: Ground-truth field agronomist observation, validated flux tower data, or authoritative agricultural survey
provenance_requirements.label_date: Timestamp of ground inspection within +/- 3 days of satellite overpass
provenance_requirements.legal_license: Permissible for research and model training (e.g. CC-BY 4.0, Open Government License, or proprietary authorized agreement)

split_protocol.spatial_grouping: Unique field ID or Farm cluster ID (strictly no shared fields between train and test)
split_protocol.temporal_holdout: Independent growing season or terminal month holdout

known_scientific_limitations: Satellite indicators reflect radiometric surface reflectance and active microwave backscatter; they do not identify pathogens or microscopic pests without field ground-truthing.
Cloud cover and prolonged monsoon precipitation can obstruct optical passes, necessitating reliance on radar backscatter.
Irrigation events, standing surface water, and tillage induce acute dielectric jumps that must be differentiated from biological crop stress.
